title: Support a contrast, cause or prediction with two parts
subtitle: Command of Evidence · 38 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **38 of the official questions in Command of Evidence are this one** — 0 Easy, 5 Medium, 33 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- This is a harder version of the hypothetical-finding question.
- The conclusion compares two groups (X did one thing while Y did another), proposes a cause for an observed result, or predicts a future outcome from an earlier effect.
- The choices are long, and several mention both groups or both variables.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Break the conclusion into its parts: group A has property P, group B has property Q, or cause C produces effect E.
- 2) Rule out any choice that confirms only one part, and any choice that assumes the result is true without showing the proposed mechanism.
- 3) Choose the one that links the specific cause to the specific outcome, or that distinguishes the two groups in the way the conclusion needs.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You choose a finding that simply restates the observed result, or that is true of both groups equally.
Either way it doesn't separate the groups or isolate the proposed explanation, so it adds no support.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You choose a finding that simply restates the observed result, or that is true of both groups equally.
Either way it doesn't separate the groups or isolate the proposed explanation, so it adds no support.
